speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing hematuria and right flank pain; to begin our assessment, have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea accompanying these symptoms? Additionally, has this pain radiated to your groin or lower abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; given your history of recurrent urinary tract infections and visible blood in the urine, have you noticed any difficulty passing urine, such as a weak stream or the feeling that your bladder is not emptying? Also, do you have a history of kidney stones, smoking, or exposure to industrial chemicals?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming. To narrow down the cause of your hematuria and flank pain, have you noticed any foul-smelling urine or passed any small, hard objects in your urine? Additionally, do you have a history of kidney stones, smoking, or occupational exposure to chemicals? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Urolithiasis (Kidney Stone). The urinalysis shows significant hematuria with pyuria but negative nitrites, which, combined with your right flank pain and history of recurrent UTIs, strongly suggests a stone rather than a typical bacterial infection. Please request images of your right kidney and ureter to confirm the presence of a calculus.
